newsitem.title: CHINA: Mongolia approves oil deal with U.S. Nescor.
newsitem.headline: Mongolia approves oil deal with U.S. Nescor.

text.p: Mongolia has approved an oil production sharing contract with Nescor Energy Corp of Texas, giving the U.S. firm sole rights to 1.25 million acres (506,250 hectares) of the East Gobi Basin, a company statement said.

Nescor, which previously split the rights to the area with the Mongolian government under a joint exploration agreement, now has exploration and/or production rights to an area covering 13 million acres in Mongolia, the statement said.
"We are very encouraged by the results of our recent production testing and we anticipate full-scale operations to begin this summer," Nescor chief Neil Salsich said.

Nescor, based in Austin, Texas, has pioneered attempts to help Mongolia resume domestic oil production, which effectively ceased in 1965 after the Soviet Union discovered high-grade oil in Siberia and withdrew its technical experts.
Mongolian officials estimate the country may have reserves of up to 600 million barrels of oil.
Cash shortages have hampered Mongolia's ability to fund its share of joint venture projects with foreign firms, quashing early hopes for a quick resumption of production.
Under its new pact with the Mongolian Petroleum Authority, Nescor takes over the government's 50 percent rights to the acreage in blocks 13 and 14 in Mongolia's East Gobi Basin.
Last summer, Nescor conducted production tests in the Zuunbayan, Southwest Zuunbayan and Tsagaan Els fields, drilling one new well and re-entering 150 of the more than 200 dormant wells in the area.
At Tsagaan Els No. 14, production tests indicate an estimated initial potential of 800 barrels per day, the company's statement said.
